title: Odd noisy-function acceptance bound
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\\varepsilon\\in[0,1]$, let $\\rho\\in[-1,1]$ with $\\rho\\ge 0$, and suppose $\\varepsilon\\le 1-\\rho^2$. Let $f$ be a real-valued function on the sign cube with values in $[-1,1]$. For each coordinate $i$, define its stable influence at parameter $1-\\varepsilon$ by $\\sum_{S\\ni i}(1-\\varepsilon)^{|S|-1}\\widehat f(S)^2$, where $\\widehat f(S)$ is the uniform Fourier coefficient. If every such stable influence is at most $\\varepsilon$, then the original three-query BLR tester accepts the odd part of the $\\rho$-noise of $f$ with probability at most $\\frac12+\\frac{\\sqrt{\\varepsilon}}2$.
